All files are revised in place; nothing else is pending. Summary of the planted issues:

The matter is a self-funded ERISA plan (Halvorsen) whose TPA (Meridian) has, in Article 9 of the ASA, a consent right over sharing claims data with consultants/auditors (all defined as "Competitors"), a bar on the sponsor disclosing provider-specific rates to participants and referring providers, a 250-claim/once-a-year/view-only audit cap, and a "custom extract" regime that strips the statutory per-claim fields (allowed amounts, provider NPI/name) out of standard access, prices them at ~$140–160k with a 180-day lag from an undated "acceptance," and reserves a right to decline anything revealing "Proprietary Information" (defined to include allowed amounts) — all under a savings clause the TPA claims cures everything. The revised task now also plants: (i) an upstream Continental–Meridian network-license clause (§ 4.3) that is the real source of the restrictions and requires the carrier's consent to fix; (ii) a Northgate data request that is not safe-harbor de-identified (full dates of service) and a plan-document § 164.504(f) firewall that the CFO's request to circulate the raw file to the Committee would breach; (iii) a three-month Cordell-era gap in the requested period that Meridian cannot supply; (iv) a conflicted consultant (contingent $150k transition fee, undisclosed Marketplace fees) raising ERISA § 408(b)(2)(B); (v) the IRC § 4980D mechanics the CFO asked for — the $500,000 reasonable-cause cap and the likely-expired 30-day correction window — rather than a $100/day headline; plus the retained traps (de-identification is about participants, § 12.4 changes-in-law doesn't apply to a 2020 statute, the plan not the TPA is the regulated party, the non-renewal window has passed, the two prior unqualified attestations, the December 31 attestation must still be filed with an Additional Information disclosure, and § 12.5/§ 9.8 reaching a successor TPA). The rubric grew from 22 to 32 criteria, with new negative criteria for the PHI-to-Committee error and for invented regulations/penalties, and sharpened criteria (c01, c05, c17, c19, c22) so that the previously trivial passes now require specific synthesis.
